objectives.goal: Name core home spaces and locate a person or object inside one.
Distinguish presence from absence and change the noun after nėra.
Use plural naming forms and selected d→dž / t→č stem changes.
objectives.limit: Samples selected noun classes; this does not establish every Lithuanian plural or stem alternation.

objectives.goal: Match number gender and contrast naming plurals after two with genitive plurals after ten/kiek.
Ask for a floor location and distinguish it from a room number.
objectives.limit: Floor location has a new-context check; room-number questions currently have repeated retrieval and supported reading only.

objectives.goal: Agree adjectives and description questions with masculine/feminine nouns.
Use ant/prie/tarp/vidury with familiar objects and genitive forms.
Distinguish a needed object from a needed action, and wanting from having to act.
objectives.limit: New-context checks sample obligation and noun need; infinitive need is practised with repeated bounded prompts.

objectives.goal: Ask permission for one's own action versus asking another person politely.
Report missing hot water and ask for help with a repair.
objectives.limit: Choice-based social replies; future repair timing is introduced as a chunk, not a complete tense lesson.

objectives.goal: Ask about rooms, floor, internet and rent; compare information in adverts.
objectives.limit: Prepared reply choices and visible-text comprehension, not spontaneous negotiation or listening to a price.

objectives.goal: Invite a guest in, offer a seat and respond to a request.
objectives.limit: Hosting phrases are bounded chunks. Wider invitations remain in the retained scaffold; independent transfer is not established.

objectives.goal: Write a short rental enquiry using the taught questions.
objectives.limit: Saved and self-reviewed; no automatic grammar or communicative-success score.

lessons.title: A flat, a room and a kitchen
lessons.goal: Learn the places you will ask about when viewing a flat.

steps.title: Start with the home
steps.note: Butas is a flat or apartment. Kambarys is a room; virtuvė is a kitchen. First learn the names, then use their location forms.

steps.correction: Compare the pairs in the example.

lessons.title: Say where you are
lessons.goal: Use in the flat, in the room and in the kitchen.

steps.title: One person, three locations
steps.note: A location needs no preposition: butas → bute, kambarys → kambaryje, virtuvė → virtuvėje. Virtuvėje follows the same pattern as kavinėje in the previous chapter.

lessons.title: Arrange a viewing
lessons.goal: Recall a meeting point, day and time before asking about a flat.

lessons.title: There is a table—or there isn’t
lessons.goal: Change the noun form when saying something is absent.

steps.title: Keep the object the same
steps.note: Yra uses the naming form stalas. Nėra uses stalo, the genitive. The missing object is still a table; the sentence changes its form.

steps.correction: Nėra means there is no; the noun becomes stalo.

steps.title: The same contrast with a chair
steps.note: With a noun ending in -ė, the absent-object form ends in -ės: kėdė → kėdės.

steps.correction: After yra, use the naming form stalas.

lessons.title: One object or several
lessons.goal: Recognize the plural before combining it with a number.

steps.title: The plural forms
steps.note: For these naming forms: -as becomes -ai, -ė becomes -ės, and -ys becomes -iai. Kėdės can also mean of a chair after nėra; the surrounding sentence tells you its role.

steps.correction: Stalai is plural; stalas is singular.
Kambariai is plural; kambarys is singular.
Kėdės is the naming form for chairs.

lessons.title: Two tables, two chairs
lessons.goal: Keep the number the same and match it to the noun’s gender.

steps.title: Two has two forms
steps.note: Stalas and kambarys are masculine, so use du. Kėdė is feminine, so use dvi. The number still means two; the noun determines its form.

lessons.title: Ask how many rooms
lessons.goal: Ask for a count and understand the answer.

steps.title: The question and the answer use different forms
steps.note: When asking how many rooms, use kiek + genitive plural: kambarių. In the answer, du takes the plural naming form kambariai.

steps.correction: After kiek when asking how many: kambarių.

lessons.title: Ask which floor

steps.title: Naming the floor
steps.note: Both words change for a location: pirmas aukštas → pirmame aukšte.

steps.title: Which floor?
steps.note: The question and answer both use location forms: kelintame aukšte / antrame aukšte. Antras becomes antrame.

steps.correction: On the first floor: pirmame aukšte.

lessons.title: Ask whether there is internet

steps.title: Ask about a facility

steps.title: Mirror: change the ending and stem

steps.title: The same object, two messages

steps.correction: Reikia expresses a need, not just absence.

steps.title: A towel
steps.note: Rankšluostis becomes rankšluosčio: t changes to č before -io. Learn this exact form with the noun; do not just remove its ending.

steps.title: A noun ending in -ius

lessons.goal: Describe a position relative to one or two familiar objects.

steps.title: Between two objects
pairs: Between the table and the bed.
Kėdė yra tarp stalo ir lovos.
The chair is between the table and the bed.

lessons.title: May I—or can you
lessons.goal: Change who will open the same window.

steps.title: Open the window
steps.note: Atidaryti and uždaryti are infinitives: to open and to close. Langas becomes langą as the object of the action.

steps.title: Who will do the action?
steps.note: Galiu means I can; galite addresses you politely. The action atidaryti stays unchanged. Ar galiu asks permission for your own action; ar galite asks the other person to act.

steps.correction: You want permission for your own action: galiu.
You ask the other person to act: galite.

lessons.title: Need an object or an action
lessons.goal: Follow reikia with a noun or with an infinitive.

steps.title: The need can be an action
pairs: The window needs to be closed.
steps.note: A needed object uses genitive: kompiuterio. A needed action uses an infinitive: uždaryti. The action still has its own object, langą.

options: The window needs to be closed.
answers: The window needs to be closed.
steps.correction: Reikia expresses a need; it does not ask permission.

steps.translation: The window needs to be closed.
steps.correction: The needed action is to close: uždaryti.

steps.title: Want to or have to
pairs: I want to tidy the room.
I have to tidy the room.
steps.note: Tvarkyti means to tidy. Noriu expresses a wish; turiu + infinitive expresses an obligation. Keep tvarkyti kambarį the same and change only the meaning of the first verb.

steps.translation: I have to tidy the room.
steps.correction: Turiu + infinitive means I have to.

steps.translation: The window needs to be closed.
I have to tidy the room.
I want to tidy the room.

steps.note: A room number names the room: dvyliktas kambarys. A floor location uses kelintame aukšte, with both words in the location form. Dvyliktas means twelfth, used here to identify room twelve.

steps.correction: Kambarys identifies the room; aukštas is the floor.
Use naming form kelintas with kambarys.
Use location form kelintame with aukšte.

lessons.title: Welcome a guest
lessons.goal: Invite someone in and respond to a request.

steps.title: Two invitations
steps.note: These are useful hosting phrases. Prašom introduces a polite invitation. Taip, žinoma accepts a request.

steps.correction: Sėstis invites the person to sit down.

steps.title: A polite refusal
steps.note: You can grant a request with taip, žinoma or decline it with ne, atsiprašau.

lessons.title: Choose a flat from two adverts
lessons.goal: Combine room count, internet and floor information.

steps.source: You need two rooms and internet. Which flat fits?
steps.correction: A has two rooms and internet. B has three rooms and no internet.

A
Du kambariai. Yra internetas. Butas antrame aukšte. Nuoma: 450 €.

B
Trys kambariai. Nėra interneto. Butas pirmame aukšte. Nuoma: 400 €.

steps.source: You want the first floor. Does that flat have internet?

lessons.title: Read a reply about a repair
lessons.goal: Understand the timing of a repair and a softer request for help.

steps.title: A short repair message
pairs: He will be here in the afternoon.
steps.note: Gal softens the request. Kviečiu says I am calling. Learn bus po pietų as a useful future-time message here; the wider future-tense pattern comes later.

options: He will be here in the afternoon.
answers: He will be here in the afternoon.
steps.correction: Po pietų means in the afternoon; bus refers to a future time.

lessons.title: Ask about a rental
lessons.goal: Write a short enquiry about a flat you might rent.

steps.instruction: Write a short enquiry about a flat you might rent.
steps.sample: Laba diena. Noriu išsinuomoti butą. Kiek kambarių yra bute? Kelintame aukšte jis yra? Ar yra internetas? Kiek kainuoja nuoma?
checklist: Say you want to rent a flat.
Ask about rooms, floor, or price.
Ask whether a facility you need is present.
steps.hint: Use short sentences and check each point in the list.
steps.correction: Compare your message with the example.
